summary.oneLiner: Viceroy Hotels delivered a 35.3% Q4 revenue surge driven by the consolidation of Marriott Executive Apartments, masking a softer underlying organic trend due to geopolitical headwinds. The core investment thesis hinges on a INR 100cr+ renovation program already driving 20-22% ADR uplifts in renovated inventory, with FY27 poised for margin expansion as convention center upgrades complete and debt stabilizes post-acquisition.

one-line thesis: Viceroy Hotels delivered a 35.3% Q4 revenue surge driven by the consolidation of Marriott Executive Apartments, masking a softer underlying organic trend due to geopolitical headwinds. The core investment thesis hinges on a INR 100cr+ renovation program already driving 20-22% ADR uplifts in renovated inventory, with FY27 poised for margin expansion as convention center upgrades complete and debt stabilizes post-acquisition.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 49.5cr Q4 (+35.3% YoY), INR 149.7cr FY26 (+6.3% YoY); EBITDA: INR 15.6cr Q4 (+43.7% YoY, 31.4% margin), INR 44.6cr FY26 (+20.6% YoY, 29.8% margin); PAT: INR 6cr Q4 (down ~40% YoY due to deferred tax reversal in prior year base + higher finance/depreciation); Order Book: N/A (Service); Net Debt: INR 264cr (up from near-zero, funded MEA acquisition). One-offs: Prior year PAT inflated by deferred tax asset recognition on NCLT losses; Current PAT pressured by INR 5.3cr finance cost (vs INR 0.64cr prior) and depreciation from new assets/renovations.
guidance: Revenue: Double-digit growth expected FY27 (organic 5-7% + renovation driven); Margin: EBITDA to expand via convention center completion (targeting 2x EBITDA from MICE) and backend efficiencies; Order Inflow: N/A; Capex/Commissioning: Convention center renovation completes FY27 (1.5yr payback); Phase 2 (Marriott) completes FY27; Phase 3 completes FY28; Madhapur greenfield opens FY29-30.
order book & pipeline: N/A - Service sector; however, renovation pipeline includes INR 100cr+ committed capex across 3 phases with Phase 1 (Courtyard) complete, Phase 2 (Marriott) underway (Apr '26 start), and Phase 3 targeted for FY28.
segment / subsidiary detail: Hotels (Marriott/Courtyard): Room rev 55-60%, F&B 35-40%; F&B margins 45-50%. Extended Stay (MEA): Room rev 64-65%, F&B 32-33%; Higher EBITDA contribution due to limited F&B overhead. MEA Q4 Rev: INR 12.7cr (Room INR 9cr + F&B INR 3.7cr). Seasonality: Q3/Q4 occupancy 80%+ (peaking 90%); Q1/Q2 ~70%.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Convention Center expansion (20k sq ft) expected to double MICE EBITDA upon FY27 completion. 2) Madhapur greenfield project (pure room play, high GOP) targeting FY29/30 opening in supply-scarce IT corridor. 3) Distressed asset acquisitions (NCLT) under evaluation, though deal flow currently thin due to sector strength. 4) ADR upside: Targeting INR 9,000-9,500 short-term (vs current ~INR 7,600) and INR 10,000 long-term via refurbishment (20-22% uplift) + organic growth (5-7%).
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded 183bps QoQ to 31.4% driven by high-margin MEA consolidation and Phase 1 renovation efficiencies. Cost saves: Laundry outsourced (cost down 35-40%), HVAC upgrades reducing power costs, shared back-office functions across 3 properties. F&B gross margin ~85%, operating margin 45-50%.
capex / expansion: INR 100cr+ phased renovation program ongoing. Specific convention center renovation started April '26, completion expected by end of CY '26/FY '27. Greenfield Madhapur project in land conversion stage. Funding via existing debt (INR 264cr) and internal accruals; no further debt increase anticipated.
capital allocation: Priority 1: Complete asset enhancement (renovations) to drive ADR/mix. Priority 2: Debt servicing (currently comfortable at INR 264cr). Priority 3: Greenfield development (Madhapur). Dividends: Management targets resumption by FY27 end post-convention center completion and stabilization.
risks & watch-items: 1) Geopolitical tensions impacting travel sentiment (noted in March '26 softness). 2) Execution risk on renovation timelines delaying ADR upside. 3) Interest rate sensitivity on INR 264cr debt. 4) Potential supply surge in Hyderabad by FY30-31 (though management sees delays in competitor projects). 5) Customer mix cyclicality (group vs transient) during convention center downtime.
management quality / tone: Confident and execution-focused; acknowledges near-term geopolitical headwinds but emphasizes structural demand and supply scarcity. Transparent on debt increase for MEA acquisition and PAT distortion due to prior year tax adjustments. Aggressive on ADR targets (25-30% total growth potential) and cost rationalization.
non-obvious takeaways: 1) 65% of current occupancy comes from Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, reducing OTA commission drag (targeting 80-85%). 2) Legacy management contracts signed in 2006/2008 provide favorable terms vs new market entrants. 3) Courtyard occupancy dip to 52% in FY26 was entirely renovation-driven and has already normalized to ~95-99% for new inventory. 4) MEA segment has virtually no new supply pipeline in Hyderabad, creating a moat for extended-stay pricing.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply scarcity in Hyderabad premium segment combined with Viceroy's aggressive renovation-driven ADR uplift (targeting 25-30% growth) positions them to outperform peers facing flat pricing. | Viceroy Hotels Limited | beneficiary | High | Consolidation of high-margin MEA assets and imminent completion of convention center renovations create a visible earnings inflection point for FY27, while debt levels are deemed manageable post-acquisition. |

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Portfolio is entirely Marriott-branded and Hyderabad-concentrated: Marriott Hyderabad (prime location near Hussain Sagar, near business districts and tourist attractions), Courtyard by Marriott (access to business hubs, IT corridor and airports; proximity to convention and MICE venues) and Marriott Executive Apartments (located in Hyderabad's IT & finance corridor, 'ideal for long-stay corporate & expatriates').
- Stated vision is 'to transform Asia's hospitality landscape, aiming to be a top brand'.
- The deck frames Hyderabad as a structurally tight market: 7,600 branded keys across 48 hotels, premium hotels 66% of supply vs Upper Midscale-to-Economy 34%, and 'strong corporate demand' supported by a GCC hub of around 355 capability centers.
- Industry backdrop cited is a demand-supply mismatch — All India demand CAGR 10.4% (FY24-FY28F) against supply 8.5% (FY24-FY28F).
- Promoter pedigree is presented as a differentiator: MD & CEO Ravinder Reddy Kondareddy (Anirudh Group, 500+ acres of real estate assets across AP, Telangana and Karnataka) and director S.P. Reddy, who owned franchises of Marriott International, Hilton, InterContinental, Choice, Cendant and Best Western in North America.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Acquired Marriott Executive Apartments in Hyderabad — Consideration INR 206 Cr (excl. Stamp duty cost); Location SLN Terminus, Gachibowli, Hyderabad; Keys 75 Executive Rooms (1,65,000 sq. ft); Land Share 2,400 sq. Yds (approx.); CY25 Turnover INR 48.08 Cr (Calendar Year); CY25 EBITDA INR 21.45 Cr (operational EBITDA).
- [Hyderabad infrastructure] Deck lists catalysts with timelines: Regional Ring Road (faster intercity travel, 2026), NH-65 Double-Decker Corridor (2026), Metro Rail Phase II incl. Airport Express (by 2030), Pharma City at Mucherla (by 2030) and a proposed New Airport at Kothagudem (TBD).
- [Demand shock flagged] Annexure note: 'The war and geopolitical tensions in March exerted downward pressure on hospitality demand, leading to softer performance across ADR, occupancy, and RevPAR.'
- [Management build-out] A largely new senior team is presented — COO Pradyumna Kodali (ex-OYO, ex-Credit Suisse), CFO Venkata Krishna Reddy Puli (CA, 15+ years), and two Addl. CEOs from BBR Infra covering Engineering and Procurement/HR.
